name: com.midasiteurope/civil-nx
title: MIDAS CIVIL NX tools (MIDAS IT Europe)
description: Build, check and report on MIDAS CIVIL NX bridge models and design tendons, with MIDAS IT plugins.

tools.name: analysis_diagnose
tools.description: Use when the analysis stops or warns ("DOF may be singular", "error norm is infinite / NaN", convergence not reached, run-time errors): pass the message text. It names the nodes and stages with free DOFs, the cause and the fix. For a general review of the model use model_health_check. Finds why a CIVIL NX analysis stopped or warned ("DOF may be singular", "error norm is infinite / NaN", "displacement abnormal", "has not satisfied convergence tolerance", "beam section temperature cannot be applied", run-time errors) or gives results that look like a mechanism. Pass the message lines in message (the API does not return them). The tool recognises the message and says what it means, then reads the open model and finds, node by node, the degrees of freedom nothing stiffens — only trusses / solids / plane-stress elements at a node (no rotation), only plates (no drilling rotation), every beam end released, a node hanging on an elastic link with no stiffness, a node with no element — and the parts that can move as a rigid body (a mechanism: a deck sliding on its bearings, a member spinning about its axis, a part hanging off a truss), each with what holds it and the fix (including the Main Control Data switches 'Auto Rotational DOF Constraint' and 'Auto Normal Rotation Constraint for plates'). The same scan runs at the end of every construction stage, so a stage that floats is named. It also runs the health checks that bear on the message (support adequacy, disconnected parts, release mechanisms, links, stage supports…), lists tension/compression-only parts when a case does not converge, and returns the support FAQ answers for the message. Without a message it scans the whole model. Read-only (GET /db). For a full model review use model_health_check.

message.description: The analysis message(s) as CIVIL NX printed them, e.g. 'WARNING : NODE NO. 123 RZ DOF MAY BE SINGULAR'. Several lines are fine.

nodes.description: Node numbers to examine (those in the message are taken automatically).

stage.description: Construction stage to examine in detail (a stage named in the message is taken automatically). Default: all stages, five examples each.

tools.name: auto_structure_groups
tools.description: Use to group elements automatically by section, material or both. For groups by position or by construction-stage segment use stage_groups; for one group of ids you already know use civil_write_tables (GRUP). Creates one structure group per section, per material, or per section + material pair, with the Auto Structure Groups plugin's own engine: it reads every element's section and material, names each group from the prefix and the section/material names (cleaned and cut to 40 characters, as in the plugin; elements with no section/material go to <prefix>UNASSIGNED), largest group first. Optional: include each group's nodes, skip groups with fewer than minElements elements, or write only the groups named in groups. A name that already exists is skipped unless existing: 'overwrite' — and then this run's members are ADDED to that group (CIVIL NX merges a write into an existing group; it never removes members). Previews unless apply: true with confirmPlanHash; the plugin's writer re-reads db/GRUP, writes in batches and checks the read-back. auto_structure_groups_undo reverses it.

mode.description: What one group holds: one section, one section + material pair, or one material.

prefix.description: Put in front of every group name.

includeNodes.description: Also put each group's element nodes in the group.

minElements.description: Skip groups with fewer elements than this (2 or more turns the filter on).

groups.description: Write only these proposed groups (names from the preview); default all.

existing.description: A proposed name that already exists: leave that group alone, or add this run's members to it.

apply.description: Write to CIVIL NX. Only after the user approved the preview.

confirmPlanHash.description: planHash from the approved preview; the write is refused if the plan differs.

tools.name: b2p_survey
tools.description: Use before b2p_convert, to see which beams and sections can become a plate or solid mesh. To read a section's shape use section_read; for bar placement in a design check use ec2_describe_section or cs455_describe_section. Reads the model the way the Beam to Plate plugin (1.0.6) does and studies every section the chosen beams use, against CIVIL NX's own published properties (/ope/SECTPROP): whether the outline was READ correctly (A/Iyy/Izz vs published) and how far the PLATE model sits from it, the verdict (converts / blocked / not read, with the reason), the plugin's plate-or-solid suggestion with the mesh a solid would need, material slots of composite parts, the model's length/force units, the beams that cannot be converted and why, and an element estimate for the mesh. Choose beams with ONE of elementIds, sections, groups or useCivilSelection (default: every beam). Read-only; on the website it runs as a background job (poll job_status).

tools.name: b2p_convert
tools.description: Use to replace beam elements with a plate or solid mesh of their real cross-section (a detailed local model). Not for building a new deck (skew_grillage) or changing spans (bridge_reshape). Converts beam elements into a plate (or solid) mesh of their cross-section with the Beam to Plate plugin's own engine (1.0.6): every section CIVIL NX gives geometry for (rolled/fabricated steel, PSC, boxes, composite, tapered groups, VALUE, catalogue), solid concrete sections as a grid of plates or as solids, exact beam loads / nodal loads / temperatures moved onto the mesh, haunches, diaphragms, deck slabs joined, rigid links to whatever else meets the beam's nodes (staged per construction stage), virtual beams per row of plates, groups and composite casting stages carried across. Previews by default (totals, volume check, per-section verdict, notes, what is left behind such as tendons or lanes, problems, planHash) and writes nothing. With apply: true and confirmPlanHash it re-reads the model, refuses if the plan changed, and writes the plugin's way: nodes, thicknesses and elements written and read back, then links, loads, groups, stages, virtual beams, and only then the source beams deleted (deleteSourceBeams); a write that fails part way is rolled back by the plugin. The run is recorded for b2p_undo. Lengths are in the model's unit. Use b2p_survey first. Runs as a background job on the website (poll job_status).

tools.name: bridge_reshape_read
tools.description: Use before bridge_reshape, to see the existing bridge's spans, skews, alignment and levels. Read-only. Reads the open model the way the Bridge Reshaper plugin (1.0.6) does: the deck (straight, in straight pieces kinked at half-joints or piers, or curved; beam girders, girders meshed as plates, or a spine (single-line) model with its pylons, stays and piers read as substructure; any length unit), its spans, supports and skews (Abutment A, Pier 1…, Abutment B, skew in degrees from square), girder/edge lines, bearings and substructure assemblies, its direction (tightest radius on a curve) and its levels (level at each abutment, grade, cross slope), with a plan drawing. Read-only; on the website it runs as a background job (poll job_status). Use it before bridge_reshape.

axis.description: Spans run along global X or Y. Default: X, or Y when no deck is found along X (the read says which it used).

deckGroups.description: Structure groups that ARE the deck, when the automatic choice is wrong. Default: found from the model.

picture.description: Return a plan drawing (PNG) to look at.

supports.description: Where the supports are, chosen instead of the ones found — when the plugin finds none (bearings it cannot read) or finds every construction-stage support defined. Each: ch = chainage along the deck from where its girders start (model unit), skew in degrees from square. At least the two ends. bridge_reshape_read reports the girders' extent and the supports it found.

tools.name: bridge_reshape
tools.description: Use to change the spans, support skews, alignment or deck levels of a bridge that is already in the model. For a new deck use skew_grillage; for geometry from a drawing use dxf_import. Changes the geometry of the bridge in the open model in place, with the Bridge Reshaper plugin's own engine (1.0.6): new span lengths (the deck is stretched - each span keeps its element count), a skew for each support, a new horizontal alignment (straight, segments, fitted points, LandXML/DXF) and new deck levels (flat, grades with parabolic vertical curves, one-way or crowned cross slope). crossMembers 'parallel' (default) moves nodes only - every element, node, load, group, stage and lane keeps its id; 'square' re-meshes the deck with cross members square to the girders running on to the skewed support lines (straight decks of beam girders only, not with new levels). Loads, structure groups, construction stages, lanes, tapered groups and links follow the deck; beam loads in global axes, plane loads and lane end skews are turned with it; piers and abutments follow their supports ('follow' the skew, or 'rigid' keep their shape). Previews by default: the changes, the issues and a plan drawing (grey = as it is, blue = proposed), with a planHash; nothing is written. With apply: true and confirmPlanHash it re-reads the model, refuses if anything changed since the preview, writes, reads every written node and element back, and records the run for bridge_reshape_undo. Lengths and chainages in the model's unit. Use bridge_reshape_read first. Runs as a background job on the website (poll job_status).

spans.description: New length of every span, Abutment A first (model unit). Default: as modelled.

addToEverySpan.description: Instead of spans: add this to every span.

skews.description: New skew of every support in degrees from square, Abutment A first; null keeps one. Default: as modelled.

skewAll.description: Instead of skews: the same skew at every support.

substructure.description: follow: piers and abutments shear with their support's skew; rigid: they keep their shape and turn with it.

alignment.description: A new horizontal alignment (default: as modelled - a curved deck keeps its curve). straight: a straight line through the deck start, at the deck's start heading or headingDeg (straightens a curved deck). segments: straights, arcs and clothoid transitions from the deck start, along the deck. points: a curve fitted to X,Y points (model coordinates unless keepCoordinates: false): spline through them, or a least-squares arc or polynomial. landxml / dxf: the file's text. The deck line that follows it is the centreline unless followLine names a girder/edge line (index from bridge_reshape_read).

headingDeg.description: straight: plan direction in degrees from global X (anticlockwise).

radius.description: arc: radius; spiral: radius at its start (omit = from straight).

radiusEnd.description: spiral: radius at its end (omit = to straight).

index.description: landxml / dxf: which alignment in the file (default 0).

keepCoordinates.description: points / landxml / dxf: use the coordinates as given (true) or place the curve's start at the deck start along the deck (false).

chStart.description: Chainage along the alignment where the deck starts. Default: just far enough that a skewed deck start lies on it.

tools.name: bridge_thermal_calc
tools.description: Use for code temperature values of a bridge (EN 1991-1-5, CS 454, BS 5400-2) without touching the model. To write them use bridge_thermal_apply; for a temperature you already know use civil_loads_supports (temperature). Calculates bridge temperature actions with the Bridge Thermal Loads plugin's own engine: shade air and effective bridge temperatures, the uniform ranges ΔT_N,con / ΔT_N,exp (and bearing ranges), the vertical temperature difference (linear Approach 1 or the non-linear code profile, as depth/temperature points), CS 454 / BS 5400 combined X − Y values, and the simultaneity combinations, each with its clause. Codes: EN 1991-1-5 + UK NA (default) or CEN, CS 454, BS 5400-2:2006 / 1978. Needs no model.

tools.name: bridge_thermal_apply
tools.description: Use to write code-derived bridge temperature load cases (EC1T_…) on the deck. For a single temperature value you already have, civil_loads_supports (temperature) is simpler. Temperatures are converted to the model's unit; the model is re-checked before writing, an undo record is kept before the first change, and every row is read back. Previews unless apply: true.

tools.name: bridge_thermal_remove
tools.description: Use to delete every EC1T_ thermal load case, whichever run or window wrote it. To reverse one run only use bridge_thermal_undo; for other loads use civil_remove_loads. Removes what the Bridge Thermal Loads plugin writes: every load case whose name starts with EC1T_ (also named sets and ones the plugin window wrote) and all temperature loads in them, on any element. Other load cases are not touched. An undo record is kept, so bridge_thermal_undo can put them back. Previews unless apply: true.

tools.name: concurrent_forces_setup
tools.description: Concurrent forces, step 1: use before concurrent_forces to list the items, effects and load states the model offers. Read-only. Concurrent Force Reporter, step 1. Reads the open CIVIL NX model the way the plugin does when it connects and lists what a concurrent-forces run can use: every load case and combination (all ten LCOM tables) with how MIDAS addresses it, whether it is envelope-valued, and whether it is AVAILABLE — moving load, settlement, response spectrum, ABS and SRSS (anywhere down the combination tree) cannot give a coexistent state and are listed with the reason and the workaround; the items the model has per result source (beam/truss/plate elements, general/elastic links, node reactions/displacements); the key effects available for them (keyEffect ids such as BEAM:Moment-y, REACTION:FZ, ELASTICLINK:Axial, with units); structure groups (element and node ranges, links found on their nodes); construction stages with their step tokens; criteria and output positions; the model's units; whether results are published. Read-only. Use search to narrow a long case list; includeConstituents shows each combination's children.

search.description: Only load cases / combinations whose name contains this (case-insensitive).

includeConstituents.description: List each combination's children (name, factor, analysis kind).

limit.description: At most this many load case entries.

units.description: Units to report in (MIDAS converts). Default: the model's own.

tools.name: concurrent_forces
tools.description: Use for the forces that act together with the extreme of ONE effect (e.g. My max with its concurrent N and Vz). For which load cases make up a combination use combination_contributions; for plain result rows use preview_result_table. Concurrent Force Reporter, step 2. For a set of items (elements, nodes, links), finds the load state that makes ONE key effect extreme at ONE key item (max, min or absolute max over the selected load cases and combinations, at every output point), then reports every item's results IN THAT SAME STATE — the coexistent forces a bearing, pier cap or connection check needs, not each item's own envelope. If the governing load is an envelope (or an Add containing one), it is resolved recursively to a single deterministic state (a weighted sum of static/stage cases, pinning each envelope to the child that governs at the key item), re-read at that state, and gated against the value MIDAS itself reports; it refuses rather than approximates. Near-ties are reported. Items: items in set syntax — elements 12 or 15to20, nodes N12, general links L12, elastic links EL12 (a range keeps only ids that exist) — and/or structure groups. keyItem must be in the set. Values come back in the units asked for (default the model's); plate results are per unit length. Read-only (only /post/TABLE result reads). Call concurrent_forces_setup first for names and keyEffect ids. Runs as a job on the website.

tools.name: concurrent_forces_probe
tools.description: Use only to diagnose why concurrent_forces finds no results for a source; not a result reader. Concurrent Force Reporter diagnostics. For each result source the plugin reads (beam, truss, plate, general link, elastic link, node reaction, node displacement), asks this CIVIL NX build with one item of that kind which table token answers, the columns it returns and how they map, the output-point tokens, and the result series published. Use it when concurrent_forces reports a missing table, column or series. Read-only.

tools.name: cs454_lane_layout
tools.description: Use to lay out CS 454 notional lanes on a carriageway width, with no model. For EN 1991-2 lanes use ec_lane_layout; to write lanes and vehicles use cs454_moving_loads. Lays out CS 454 notional lanes, remaining areas, footways and strips on a carriageway cross-section with the CS454 - Moving Load Wizard's own layout engine (Table 5.9a, cl 5.10, ALL model 1 single/convoy, ALL model 2, SV/HB routes and SV/HB with ALL), and lists the case groups each loading needs. Needs no model — use it to answer layout questions or to choose inputs before cs454_moving_loads.

Also level, packing, svVehicle, svPlacement, svStraddle, actualLanes, prefix…

Returns: existing (the lanes, vehicles, cases and groups already in the model, each marked if an earlier cs454_moving_loads run created it); laneKindSuggestion (LINE for beams, SURFACE for plates); deckRead (reference girder or plate edge, width, kerb offset, cross-beam group, skew — narrowed by deckFilter, reversed by trafficOtherWay); the lanes and cases the given settings would produce; config (the plugin's own settings file — pass it back as configFile); options (valid loadings, vehicles and Irish Rail trains). tools.name: cs455_describe_section
tools.description: Step 1 of a CS 455 (UK assessment) concrete section check. For a Eurocode check use ec2_describe_section; only to read or edit a section's shape use section_read. Start here when the user shares a reinforcement drawing, photo or schedule. Read from it: cover, for each face the layers (number of bars or spacing, and Ø - mm, inches or #US sizes are all accepted), side bars, links (Ø, legs, spacing); then call this tool. It reads one beam section from the open model through the shared MIDAS section library (outline checked against CIVIL NX's published properties), places the bars with the CS 455 plugin's own placement (cover to every edge) and RETURNS A DRAWING of the section with every bar placed - compare it with the user's drawing and correct rebar until they match (ask the user about anything the drawing does not show, e.g. cover). Then cs455_export_calc_sheet gives the report. Also returns what the plugin's engine derives: area, centroid, depth, usable_for_capacity, parts, the bars placed per schedule row (or why a row failed), and the model's concrete grade. Read-only.

tools.name: cs455_assess
tools.description: Use for CS 455 (UK assessment) ULS of RC beam, column, pier or pile sections. For EN 1992 use ec2_section_check; for slabs and plates use slab_assess; for stresses use stress_profile or sls_stress_check. CS 455 ULS assessment of reinforced concrete beam sections with the plugin's own engine: reads the concurrent force rows (BEAMFORCE / BEAMFORCEVBM for envelopes and moving loads, kN·m; a moving-load case from a model analysed without 'Normal + Concurrent Force' is refused as NOT CONCURRENT) at the chosen element ends for the chosen combinations, and runs every row — N–M flexure by strain-compatibility equilibrium, shear (additive approach, links optional), torsion (cl 5.17–5.27) — or, with member set to a column, pier or pile, the CS 455 Section 7 checks (N_uz, slenderness and additional moments, biaxial bending Eq 7.7.2a, bar restraint 7.6, shear 7.10.1 / Eq 7.11) — with status per row (PASS / FAIL / BLOCKED / OUTSIDE RANGE OF VALIDITY) and the utilisation of each check. Read-only. Takes a while for many rows (a job on the website).

tools.name: cs_stage_summary
tools.description: Use to list the construction stages already in the model (durations, groups activated). To create stages use construction_stages; for stage results use cs_stage_results. Reads the construction stage definition of the open CIVIL NX model with the Construction Stage Reporter plugin's engine and returns, per stage: duration and day range, the structure groups activated (with age and element count) and deactivated (with redistribution), boundary groups activated (deformed/original position) and deactivated, load groups activated/deactivated (first/last day), composite section parts (db/CSCS) that start acting, and the elements and boundary entities active after it. Also the composite sections, the whole-model summary, and the plugin's consistency checks (a group deactivated before it was activated, groups no stage uses, elements never activated, groups a stage names but the model lacks…). Read-only. elementIds: true adds the activated/deactivated element ids per stage; groups: true adds a row per group.

tools.name: cs_stage_results
tools.description: Use for construction-stage analysis results, stage by stage. For results that are not per stage use preview_result_table; for the Excel / PDF report use cs_stage_report. Reads construction-stage analysis results the way the Construction Stage Reporter plugin does (POST /post/TABLE in the construction-stage family, every stage in one query at its last step; stages after the analysis stopped carry the stage before and are flagged published:false). displacements (default on): per stage the largest resultant |D| over all nodes, its node and DX/DY/DZ, in mm; nodes:[ids] adds those nodes' displacements per stage. members: beam forces or stresses of chosen beams — per stage the max/min of a component over the beams active in it, with element, output position (I…J) and section part; detailElements:[ids] (≤20) adds the values along those beams. Units are the model's (forces/moments) and mm (displacements). series is a construction-stage result series (default Summation; listSeries: true lists what the model publishes, e.g. Dead Load, Tendon Primary, Creep Secondary). Needs a construction-stage analysis already run in CIVIL NX. Read-only; may take a minute on big models.

Construction-stage displacements (series, default Summation) are included when the analysis has been run; members (as cs_stage_results) adds one beam result component. The MP4 animation is not available here — use the plugin in CIVIL NX. Read-only, but the pictures make CIVIL NX show each stage in turn. Runs as a job.

tools.name: culvert_preview
tools.description: Step 1 of a 2D box culvert built from inputs (Eurocode). Not for bridge decks (skew_grillage). Needs no model.

tools.name: skew_grillage
tools.description: Use to create a new bridge deck (beam grillage or plate mesh) from spans, widths and skew. To change a deck already in the model use bridge_reshape; for geometry from a drawing use dxf_import. Generates a bridge deck (beam grillage or plate mesh) with the Skew Grillage Geometry Generator plugin's own engine: skew (0 = straight/square), unequal girders, plan curvature, multi-span, crossfall and vertical profile, arch grillages (circular, parabolic or elliptical, given rise), slab depth, automatic transverse section sizing and structure groups (GIRDERS, CROSS-BEAMS, END-BEAMS for the support-line members, SPAN-n, or DECK for plates). A deck can be placed by a base point and added into a model that already has a structure (addToExisting). Without apply it only previews (counts, metrics, groups, planHash). With apply: true it writes to CIVIL NX exactly as the plugin does: it refuses a model that already holds geometry unless addToExisting or replaceExisting is set, creates default material/sections/thickness where the ids are missing, and records the run for skew_grillage_undo.

The preview reads the model and shows exactly that.

tools.name: combination_tree
tools.description: Use to list the model's combinations, or show one's tree of cases and factors. Read-only. To split a result into its load cases use combination_contributions; to write combinations use civil_combinations_quick or the code tools. Load Combination Contribution Analyzer, step 1. Without name: lists the model's General-tab load combinations (LCOM-GEN) with type (ADD, ENVELOPE, ABS, SRSS), constituent count, whether it is a max/min pair, and whether it can be decomposed (refused: time-history, unknown analysis type, undefined constituents, self-reference, a constituent whose type differs from the case of that name) — plus the result tables the model has items for (BEAM, TRUSS, PLATE, ELASTICLINK, GENLINK, REACTION, DISPLACEMENT) with their components and units, structure groups, construction stages and the model's units. With name: that combination's full tree (nested combinations, factors, kinds), the effective factor of every load case over all Add paths (a case reached down several branches gets the sum of the path products), and the envelopes / ABS / SRSS inside it. Read-only.

name.description: A combination to show in full. Omit to list them all.

search.description: Only combinations whose name contains this (case-insensitive).

units.description: Units to report in (CIVIL NX converts). Default: the model's own.

tools.name: combination_contributions
tools.description: Use to find which load cases make up a combination's result at given items. For the forces that act together with an extreme use concurrent_forces. Load Combination Contribution Analyzer, step 2. Splits one or more load combinations' results at a set of items into the load cases that produced them: for every item, output point (beam I/J and intermediate points, plate nodes and centre), component and max/min, the signed contribution of each case, its share of the gross, and the governing permutation written out with factors multiplied down (e.g. 1.35*Self weight(ST) + 1.5*LM1(MV:max)). Add superposes; an Envelope is resolved to the child that governs at each item (the governing child is counted per envelope); ABS gives |f·R| shares; SRSS energy shares. Moving-load, settlement and response-spectrum cases enter at their max or min end. Construction-stage cases are read at the final stage's last step. Cases are identified by type and name together. EVERY item is recomposed and must match the value CIVIL NX reports for the combination at the same item, part, component and sense — if any does not, the run stops and nothing is reported. Returns per combination: the cases ranked by share of the gross over the run, cases zero everywhere, envelope governing counts, and the critical item (largest |value|) per component and sense with its full breakdown; rows largest |value| first; csv: true stores every row. Tables: BEAM, TRUSS, PLATE (per unit length, local axes), ELASTICLINK, GENLINK, REACTION (supported nodes only — CIVIL NX answers other nodes with a made-up total; zero reaction rows it omits are read as zero), DISPLACEMENT. Items in set syntax (elements 101to148, nodes N1toN20, general links L5, elastic links EL7) and/or structure groups (for node tables: the group's nodes plus the nodes of its elements). Read-only (only /post/TABLE reads). Runs as a job on the website.

combinations.description: One General-tab combination name, or up to 10 decomposed at the same items in the same run.

items.description: Items in set syntax, e.g. "101to148", "N9001toN9006", "EL1toEL10". Typed ids must exist and be of the table's kind; ranges keep only what fits.

groups.description: Structure group names to add to the set.

components.description: Components to decompose (table column names, e.g. Moment-y, Shear-z, FZ, DZ, Mxx). Default: all of the table's.

sense.description: For max/min-pair combinations: which end(s). Ignored for single-valued ones.

units.description: Units to report in (CIVIL NX converts). Default: the model's own.

maxRows.description: At most this many rows inline (largest |value| first).

csv.description: Also store every row with every case's contribution as a CSV and return its link.

tools.name: midas_library
tools.description: Use for valid names when writing tables: material standards and grades, section shapes and their dimension order, element and support rows. For how-to text and API fields use midas_docs_search. Structured reference for writing a CIVIL NX model through the API (civil_write_tables): the material standard names CIVIL NX knows (46 concrete standards), material fields per type, grades known to work, every user section shape with the order of its dimensions (vSIZE), catalogue section examples, plate thickness, beam / truss / plate element rows and plate STYPE codes, support constraint strings, load case / self weight / nodal load / combination rows, creep-shrinkage and strength-gain code options — each with its source: MIDAS IT's open-source midas-civil-python library (MIT), the MIDAS API manual, or behaviour measured on live CIVIL NX. Also every option list in midas-civil-python (148): the 67 static load case types, beam / pressure / plane load options, combination types, the 15 moving-load codes with their standard vehicles (Eurocode LM1–LM4 incl. UK NA SV/SOV, fatigue and rail; Indian road and rail), point springs and elastic links, temperature, tendons and prestress, construction stages, response spectrum / time history, units and result components. The grade lists inside each standard and the steel section catalogues are CIVIL NX's own and published nowhere: the answer says how to confirm one safely. Topics: overview, materials, sections (shape: one shape), thickness, elements, supports, loads, moving_loads, boundaries, temperature, tendons, construction, dynamic, units, results, time_dependent, python; search alone looks through every list and vehicle. Needs no model and no account.

search.description: With topic materials: only standards / grades containing this ("EN", "C40"). Alone or with topic search: every option list and vehicle in the library whose name or values contain it ("LM1", "SV 196", "tendon", "SRSS").

shape.description: sections: one user shape code, e.g. SB, H, B, P.

tools.name: civil_status
tools.description: Start here: checks the connection and summarises the open model. For one table's rows use civil_read_table. Checks the MAPI connection to CIVIL NX and summarises the open model: units, moving load code, row counts per table, structure/boundary/load group names, static load cases, stages, general combinations, and the most recent runs recorded for this key. Read-only. Call this first.

tools.name: civil_read_table
tools.description: Use for the raw rows of one model-input table. For analysis results use preview_result_table; for a model overview use civil_status. Reads one MIDAS database table (GET /db/<TABLE>) from the open model, e.g. NODE, ELEM, SECT, GRUP, STLD, STAG, LLAN, MVLDBS, LCOM-GEN. Returns rows keyed by id: the ids asked for, or the first `limit` rows. Read-only.

table.description: Table key, e.g. NODE, ELEM, GRUP, STAG.

ids.description: Row ids to return. Omit for the first `limit` rows.

tools.name: job_status
tools.description: Use only with a jobId that another tool returned. Status, progress and (when finished) the result of a tool call that returned a jobId. Poll every few seconds until status is done or failed.

tools.name: model_health_check
tools.description: Use for "is anything wrong with my model?". This is the full check: the Model Report's fourteen QC checks plus units, tendons, stages, moving loads and results. For a design check of a section use ec2_section_check or cs455_assess. One read-only check of the open CIVIL NX model for anything that is likely wrong, grouped into areas with a red/amber/green status each. DATA (no analysis needed): the Model Report's fourteen QC checks plus warped / badly shaped plates, plates facing the other way from their neighbours, nodes lying on an element without being joined to it (mesh cracks, beams resting on girders unconnected), beam lines that flip direction or whose beta angle jumps, material values out of range (unit slips), sections with zero area or inertia, plates with no thickness, rigid and elastic links that cannot work, supports holding nothing, self weight missing / upward / counted twice in a combination, upward dead loads, load values 1000× out of line, beam loads on plates, moving loads with no lanes or vehicles, construction stages (elements never activated, loads on parts not yet built, stages with no supports, activation order), combinations (cycles, unfactored ULS, duplicates, cases never combined), empty or unused groups, and tendons that cannot be stressed. UNITS (typing slips): creep/shrinkage and strength-gain inputs (fck in MPa typed into a kN/m² box, humidity as a fraction, notional size in mm in a metre model, shrinkage strains not × 10⁻⁶, strength not matching the linked concrete grade), tendon area / strengths / duct diameter / anchorage slip, thermal coefficients, temperatures, section depths and plate thicknesses. TENDONS: cover — every profile point placed on its girder and compared with the section's top and soffit (outside the concrete, with the likely coordinate slip: mm in a metre model or the sign of z; clear cover under 50 mm); jacking stress against min(0.8 fpk, 0.9 fp0.1k) and slips, duct area against the steel, friction μ and wobble ranges, friction loss estimated from each profile, sharp bends, profiles longer than their elements, tendons on elements that do not join up. MOVING LOADS (Eurocode EN 1991-2 and CS 454 / CS 458 rules): the moving-load code against the vehicles and cases; cases naming lanes or vehicles that do not exist, vehicles with no sub-type; duplicate names; lane widths against the code (Eurocode 3.0 m notional lanes or w/2 on 5.4–6 m; CS 454 3.0 m single / 2.5 m convoy, matched to the case's vehicle; SV lanes at least the vehicle width) with the slip named; remaining areas wide enough for another lane, ALL model 2 lane count and equal widths; lanes overlapping in one case; wheel spacing against the vehicles (BS stores a third, Eurocode the real value) and the lane; lanes off the deck (ECC sign flipped, mm in a metre model); lane element paths; Eurocode ψ — 'Ignore ψ factor' against a case named frequent / characteristic, ψ 0 or above 1, railway ψ1, and whether there are both characteristic and frequent LM1 cases; α factors (UK NA half entered), βQ and footway load; CS 458 SV speed against DAF, HB units. STAGES (set-up): creep/shrinkage links that reach no concrete or are switched off, activation ages under 1 day, too short a final stage, composite-section stages. RESULTS (when the model has been analysed): for every static load case the sum of reactions against the total applied load (equilibrium), the self-weight reaction against Σ density × element volume, displacements too large to be real (mechanisms, unit slips), and reaction symmetry on a symmetric model; on a construction-stage model, stages the analysis did not reach, stage displacements, and each stage's reactions against the weight and loads active then. Each with the numbers. Returns each check's result (pass / fail / not applicable / not run), severity, criterion and the ids involved. Reads only: GET /db tables, /ope/SECTPROP and POST /post/TABLE (REACTIONG, DISPLACEMENTG). On the website it runs as a job. Use model_qc_check for the plugin's fourteen checks alone, in another language.

parts.description: Which checks to run: data (model tables) and/or results (needs an analysed model). Default both.

tools.name: model_report_images
tools.description: Use before model_report_export, to pick the pictures for the report. Lists the CIVIL NX pictures the Model Report can put in this model's report, with their keys: FE model views (iso, plan, front, side), the applied loads of each static load case, the figures saved in the model (/db/UFIG), and the beam diagrams on offer (each static case, combination and construction-stage part × components Fx…Mw). Pick from them with model_report_export images. Read-only (GET only); nothing is rendered.

tools.name: model_report_export
tools.description: Use for the whole-model report document. For construction stages use cs_stage_report; for a design calculation sheet use ec2_export_calc_sheet or cs455_export_calc_sheet; for raw tables use export_result_tables. Builds the Model Report plugin's 'Model report' for the open CIVIL NX model — cover, contents, materials, sections (with drawings), supports and springs, load cases, combinations and loads, nodes/elements/groups appendix, cross sections, tendons, CIVIL NX pictures, the QC checks and the data sources read — and returns it as download links: html (default), xlsx, docx and/or pdf, in English, French, German, Greek or Polish. Document details (project, client, job no., revision, author, checker, date …) go on the cover. Pictures are rendered by CIVIL NX (POST /view/CAPTURE, the user's own view is left as it is): by default the isometric model view and every figure saved in the model; choose model views, load views, saved figures and beam diagrams with `images` (model_report_images lists them), and the beam diagrams' legend format (exponential/fixed, decimals) there too. Otherwise reads only (GET, plus POST /post/TABLE for tendon coordinates). Runs as a job.

Read-only; writes no file. Use it before model_to_ifc / model_to_dxf, or to sanity-check a model.

Only reads the model. Returns download links (never the file inline) and the exporter's report (sections, volumes, bridge parts, checks). tools.name: civil_loads_supports
tools.description: Use for any support, spring, release, self-weight, nodal load, UDL, pressure or temperature you can state directly. For code-derived loads use ec_wind_apply, bridge_thermal_apply, ec_moving_loads or cs454_moving_loads. The fast way to add supports, point springs, beam end releases, self-weight, nodal loads, beam UDLs, plate pressures and element temperatures: describe WHERE (structure group, id ranges, a line, a box, a coordinate, or the extreme nodes of a group) and WHAT, and the tool finds the nodes / elements and builds the CONS, CNLD, BMLD and PRES rows itself — no table lookup, no reading NODE / ELEM, no rows to write. Values are in kN and m by default (units: { force, length }) and converted to the model's units; signs follow the global axes (w: -10 with dir GZ = 10 kN/m downward). Missing load cases (STLD), load groups and boundary groups are created. Examples: supports [{ at: { group: "GIRDERS", pick: "xmin" }, type: "pinned" }, { at: { group: "GIRDERS", pick: "xmax" }, type: "roller-x" }]; udl [{ on: { group: "GIRDERS" }, case: "SIDL", w: -12.5 }]; udl with range { axis: "x", from: 10, to: 20 } loads only that stretch; nodalLoads [{ at: { nodes: "101to121by2" }, case: "Wheel", F: [0, 0, -50] }]; pressure [{ on: { group: "DECK" }, case: "Surfacing", p: -2.4 }]; springs [{ at: { group: "PIERS", pick: "zmin" }, k: [1e5, 1e5, 5e5] }]; releases [{ on: { group: "CROSS-BEAMS" }, free: "My Mz" }]; selfWeight [{ case: "SW" }]; temperature [{ on: { group: "DECK" }, case: "T+", uniform: 15, gradientZ: 10 }]. The preview is a summary — counts, ids, and total force per load case to check against the intended load. Apply with apply: true and confirmPlanHash; every row is read back. Undo with civil_write_tables_undo (same ledger). Rules kept for you: CIVIL NX keeps one nodal load per case per node, so loads landing on the same node and case are summed (also with an existing one, with a warning); an existing support on a node is replaced; existing beam loads and pressures are kept and the new ones added.

tools.name: section_preview
tools.description: Step 1 for a new section from a sketch or outline. For a section already in the model use section_read; for a code check use ec2_describe_section or cs455_describe_section. Checks a cross-section's outlines with Section Designer's own rules (closed, not self-crossing, holes inside their outline, no overlaps, materials) and returns a PNG drawing of it — the outlines, numbered input vertices, the centroid and chain dimensions — plus the extents, areas and every vertex. Use it FIRST, and LOOK at the drawing: compare it with the user's sketch (overall width and depth, slab and web thicknesses, haunches, cells) and correct misreads before computing or writing anything. Needs no model. From a sketch: read every dimension and put the outline down as vertices in y (across, right +) and z (up), in the sketch's units (default mm). Holes are separate rings inside their outline; direction of travel does not matter. Rounded corners: fillet on that vertex; arcs between vertices: bulge; round bars or ducts: { circle }. Standard shapes can use a template (i_girder, box_girder) instead of vertices. Two materials (girder + slab): one part each, in construction order, each with its material.

tools.description: Use to write a designed section into the model, after section_preview. Writes a section into the open CIVIL NX model exactly as Section Designer's Write button does: VALUE/GEN, PSC/VALU or COMPOSITE-GEN with its computed properties (CIVIL keeps them as sent), in the model's units read at the time of writing, then reads it back and compares every value sent. id defaults to the model's next free section id. Refuses unconverged results. If the id is taken it writes nothing and says by what (and how many elements use it); replacing needs replaceExisting: true — DESTRUCTIVE, only with the user's agreement. Previews unless apply: true with confirmPlanHash. Before applying, show the user the drawing (section_preview) and the properties and get their go-ahead. section_write_undo reverses it. Same section input as section_preview.

section.description: The section, read off the sketch. Axes: y across (positive right), z up, as seen in CIVIL's section dialog; put the origin anywhere convenient (e.g. bottom-left corner or soffit centre) — CIVIL's frame is applied on write.

units.description: Units of every coordinate, radius and template dimension.

type.description: One part: general = VALUE/GEN; psc = PSC/VALU (for prestressed concrete with PSC design). Two or more parts always write COMPOSITE-GEN.

parts.description: One part per material, in CONSTRUCTION ORDER (part 1 = first in place, e.g. the steel or precast girder; then the deck slab). Each composite stage i = parts 1…i.

anyOf.description: A grade: concrete "C40/50" (EN 1992 Ecm formula, ν 0.2) or steel "S355" (210 GPa, ν 0.3); or a Section Designer library id — "EN:C30/37" (EN 1992-1-1 Table 3.1 Ecm), "EN:S355", "EN:B500", UK assessment (CS 454 family) "UK:C40" (cube fcu, BS 5400-4 Table 3 Ec, as CS 455), "UK:S355" (BS 5400-3, 205 GPa), "UK:B500".
A library grade, optionally long term (concrete at half its short-term E).

reference.description: Composite only: the material every other part is transformed to (one part; default part 1).

densityRatio.description: CIVIL DENS_RATIO: this part's weight relative to part 1's material. Left out on a composite whose parts have grades, it is their unit-weight ratio (25 kN/m³ concrete, 77 kN/m³ steel); otherwise 1.

regions.description: Closed areas of this material. Regions of one part that touch are merged (Union).

bulge.description: The edge from this vertex to the next is an arc: tan(sweep/4), positive = anticlockwise (DXF convention). 1 = semicircle.

fillet.description: Round this corner with this radius.

anyOf.description: Vertices in order round the outline (either direction); closed automatically.

bulge.description: The edge from this vertex to the next is an arc: tan(sweep/4), positive = anticlockwise (DXF convention). 1 = semicircle.

fillet.description: Round this corner with this radius.

anyOf.description: Vertices in order round the outline (either direction); closed automatically.

holes.description: Voids inside this outer outline (box cells, ducts).

template.description: A Section Designer template instead of regions; lengths in the section's units. Soffit on z = 0 and centreline on y = 0, moved by at. i_girder: H depth, tw web, Bt/tft top flange width/thickness, Bb/tfb bottom flange, htw/hth top haunch width (beyond the web face)/height, hbw/hbh bottom haunch. box_girder: cells 1–3, B deck width, Bw outer width across the webs at the top (under the cantilever roots), Bs soffit width, H depth, ts top slab, tb bottom slab, tw web thickness (horizontal), tc/tr cantilever thickness at tip/root, htw/hth and hbw/hbh cell haunches (top and bottom corners). Haunches default to 0.

at.description: Where the template's soffit centre goes, [y, z].

warpingEffect.description: CIVIL's 'Consider warping effect': also computes and writes the warping constant IW, the shear centre (YS_YC, ZS_ZC = centroid − shear centre), IP and the warping function / torsion shear coefficients at the stress points (W, CXY, CXZ). Single-material sections only; use it for thin-walled open steel sections.

merge.description: Merge touching/overlapping regions of the same part.

id.description: Section id; default = next free id in the model.

replaceExisting.description: DESTRUCTIVE: overwrite the section already at id (elements using it change stiffness). Only with the user's agreement.

apply.description: Write to CIVIL NX. Only after the user approved the preview.

confirmPlanHash.description: planHash from the approved preview; the write is refused if the plan differs.

tools.name: section_read
tools.description: Use to list the model's sections, or get one's outline to edit. For a code check use ec2_describe_section or cs455_describe_section; for Beam to Plate use b2p_survey. Without id: lists the model's sections (id, name, type, whether Section Designer stores it as outlines) and the next free id. With id: returns the section as outlines in section_preview's input format, in units (default mm). A drawn section (VALUE/GEN, PSC/VALU, COMPOSITE-GEN) comes back with its stored properties; any other type (DB/User shapes, PSC guide-curve sections, steel girders with stiffeners and riveted angles, composite girders, tapered) is rebuilt by the section library and checked against the properties CIVIL NX published, with a note saying what was recovered — edit it and write it back with section_write.

at.description: Tapered sections only: station along the length, 0 = I end (default), 1 = J end.

tools.name: stage_groups
tools.description: Use to make structure groups by position (slices, segments) for staging. For groups by section or material use auto_structure_groups. Creates structure groups with the Construction Stage Wizard plugin's group builder: pick a scope of elements, split it by rules (slice along X/Y/Z into n segments or at cuts, by section, material, element type, thickness, id ranges, existing groups), name them from a template, and resolve clashes with existing groups by policy. Typical use: segments of a deck for staged construction, e.g. rules [{kind:'slice', axis:'X', mode:'count', count:8, cuts:[]}] with naming {template:'Seg_{SLICE}'}. Previews unless apply: true; the write keeps a snapshot for stages_undo.

typeFilter.description: Element types to keep (BEAM, TRUSS, PLATE, SOLID…); empty = all.

rules.description: Applied together (every combination becomes a group): {kind:'slice', axis:'X'|'Y'|'Z', mode:'count'|'cuts', count, cuts:[coords]}, {kind:'section'}, {kind:'material'}, {kind:'type'}, {kind:'thickness'}, {kind:'idRange', ranges:[{label, text}]}, {kind:'existingGroup', groups:[names]}.

naming.description: template with tokens {INDEX}, {SLICE}, {SECTION}, {MATERIAL}, {TYPE}…; prefix, suffix, pad, start.

policy.description: What to do when a group name already exists.

apply.description: Write to CIVIL NX. Only after the user approved the preview.

confirmPlanHash.description: planHash from the approved preview; the write is refused if the plan differs.

tools.name: construction_stages
tools.description: Use to create a construction stage sequence. To read the stages already defined use cs_stage_summary. Builds a construction stage sequence with the Construction Stage Wizard plugin's bulk generator and writes it with its stage planner (which keeps composite sections and construction-stage load combinations intact, rewriting and restoring them when CIVIL NX would otherwise delete them). Structure groups are activated in order, groupsPerStage at a time; boundary and load groups (e.g. supports, self weight) ride in the first new stage; an optional temporary group per stage (e.g. a form traveller) is switched on and off with it; an optional final stage closes the sequence. mode 'append' adds after the model's existing stages; 'replace' replaces them all. Every stage is validated against the model's groups first. Previews unless apply: true; the write keeps a snapshot for stages_undo.

groupPrefix.description: Instead of groups: every structure group whose name starts with this, in natural order (Seg_2 before Seg_10).

durations.description: Days per stage; several values repeat as a pattern (e.g. [7, 7, 14]). Default [7].

age.description: Material age at activation, days; null follows the stage duration.

boundaryGroups.description: Boundary groups activated in the first new stage (deformed position).

loadGroups.description: Load groups activated in the first new stage (e.g. self weight).

temporary.description: {family:'load'|'boundary', groups:[one per stage]}: on in its stage, off in the next.

finalStage.description: {name, duration, steps}: a closing stage, e.g. long-term with time steps.

naming.description: {template:'CS{INDEX}', start, pad}. In append mode start defaults to after the last existing stage.

apply.description: Write to CIVIL NX. Only after the user approved the preview.

confirmPlanHash.description: planHash from the approved preview; the write is refused if the plan differs.

tools.name: stress_element_loads
tools.description: Use before stress_profile, to see what results each beam element has. Read-only. Reads what the Stress Profile Generator can show for chosen beam elements: each element's section (type, outline verified, composite parts, tapered), material, length, the load cases / combinations / envelopes CIVIL NX publishes results for (with kind and whether each is one concurrent state), the construction stages with results for that element (and, with stage, that stage's results such as Summation). Also lists the model's combinations with the SLS category the plugin would guess. Read-only; reads results with a few batched /post/TABLE requests. Use it before stress_profile or sls_stress_check.

elements.description: Element list as the plugin takes it, e.g. "1-20, 35, 40 to 44".

group.description: A structure group; its beam elements are used.

stage.description: A construction stage: also list its results for each element.

tools.name: stress_profile
tools.description: Use for the stress distribution through ONE beam section. For SLS limits over many elements use sls_stress_check; for capacity checks use ec2_section_check or cs455_assess. The Stress Profile Generator's profile for ONE beam element: from CIVIL NX's beam forces and the true section outline it calculates σx (or σx from N / My / Mz, τ from Vz / Vy, von Mises, principal, Tresca) over the section at the chosen positions and loads, and checks every profile against CIVIL NX's own published stresses (effective PSC sections are drawn through CIVIL NX's stress points; composite sections part by part from CIVIL NX's per-part results; envelopes give CIVIL NX's values at the stress points plus the governing member or static part as a profile). Returns per profile: status (ok/unchecked/points/refused) with reasons, forces, extremes and where they occur, CIVIL NX vs calculated at stress points 1–4, per-part σx for composites, and min/max across the section at each depth. With `thermal` it gives the EN 1991-1-5 temperature stresses instead, split into total, restraint, self-equilibrating, uniform and linear parts (Type 3 heating/cooling with 100 mm surfacing, a user ΔT profile, or CIVIL NX's own section temperature; restraint free, full, axial, rotation, or CIVIL NX's forces of a load). Optional csv gives the plugin's CSV export as a download link. Read-only.

loads.description: Load case / combination / envelope names as stress_element_loads lists them; with stage, that stage's results (e.g. Summation, Dead Load).

positions.description: Positions along the element: I-end, ¼, ½, ¾ span, J-end. Default ["2/4"].

stage.description: Construction stage: use its results (last step) instead of the final state.

result.description: sx σx combined; sxN/sxMy/sxMz its parts; tVz/tVy shear; vm von Mises; s1/s2 principal; tmax; tresca.

sectionProperties.description: effective = CIVIL NX's own stresses (as the plugin's default); gross = the plugin's calculation on the section as modelled, difference stated.

unit.description: Stress unit of the results (internally kN/m²).

depthLevels.description: Levels of the through-depth table (vertex levels are added); 0 leaves it out.

thermal.description: Temperature stresses instead of load results (EN 1991-1-5 §6.1.4).

preset.description: Type 3 heating / cooling (Table B.3, 100 mm surfacing — check the National Annex), user points, or CIVIL NX's own section/element temperature of thermal.load.

points.description: preset user: [depth below the top m, ΔT °C] pairs, linear between, zero outside.

restraint.description: free (statically determinate), full, axial only, rotation only, or CIVIL NX's beam forces of thermal.load.

load.description: CIVIL NX static load case / combination for preset civil or restraint civil.

components.description: Default all: tTot total, tRes restraint, teig self-equilibrating, tUni uniform (fully restrained), tLin linear (fully restrained).

E.description: E of the element's material, kN/m², if the model's is not to be used.

alphas.description: α per section part, 1/°C (null = from the model). Composite-General parts have none in the model and need it.

csv.description: Also return the plugin's CSV export of every profile (a download link).

tools.name: sls_stress_check
tools.description: Use for SLS stress limits over many elements (EN 1992-2, EN 1993-2). For one element's profile use stress_profile; for ULS capacity use ec2_section_check. The Stress Profile Generator's SLS report check (EN 1992-2 §7.2 concrete, EN 1993-2 §7.3 structural steel; normal stress σx at the fibres) over many elements × positions × combinations — or, with source stages, its construction-stage checks (fck(t) from CIVIL NX's concrete age, steel fy/γM0, tendons from CIVIL NX's tendon stresses). Every state is generated and matched with CIVIL NX as in stress_profile; composite parts are checked against their own concrete's fck. LIMITS ARE OPT-IN exactly as in the plugin: with no limit chosen the verdict is NO LIMIT APPLIED; nothing that could not be evaluated passes (INCOMPLETE). Combination categories (characteristic / frequent / quasi-permanent / none) are taken as given, else guessed from the name and reported. Returns the one verdict, the limits used, counts, the governing state, failures, what was not evaluated and why, per combination/stage and per element, and the plugin's SLS CSV as a download link. Read-only.

elements.description: Element list as the plugin takes it, e.g. "1-20, 35, 40 to 44".

group.description: A structure group; its beam elements are used.

combinations.description: source combinations: the combinations to check, each a name or {name, category}.

positions.description: Positions along the element: I-end, ¼, ½, ¾ span, J-end. Default all five.

limits.description: Combination checks. Nothing optional is on unless set here. Stresses in MPa.

fck.description: Concrete fck (used where the model holds none, or everywhere with fckForEveryConcrete).

fy.description: Structural steel fy; default from the grade name (e.g. S355).

compressionCharacteristic.description: σc ≤ k1·fck in characteristic combinations: XD/XF/XS exposure (EN 1992-2 §7.2(102)) or a project requirement.

compressionQuasiPermanent.description: σc ≤ k2·fck in quasi-permanent combinations (linear creep) — the plugin's default.

tension.description: Concrete tension rule per category: none (default) | fctm | zero (decompression) | user.

steel.description: Characteristic steel check: |σx| ≤ fy/γM,ser, or full (+ τ and von Mises, elementary shear, no torsion).

stageLimits.description: source stages. The plugin's defaults: compression on (kc 0.6), tension none, steel full, tendons checked.

testedFckEarly.description: Tested fck for ages ≤ 3 d (EN 1992-1-1 §3.1.2(5)); without it those states are not evaluated.

unit.description: Stress unit of the results (internally kN/m²).

csv.description: Return the plugin's SLS CSV (every state, one row per part) as a download link.

tools.name: civil_write_tables
tools.description: Use for a model change no other tool makes (e.g. building from scratch). Prefer civil_loads_supports for loads and supports, civil_combinations_quick for combinations, and a plugin tool where one fits. Creates, changes or deletes rows in any CIVIL NX database table through the MIDAS API — nodes, elements, materials, sections, thicknesses, supports, links, load cases, loads, groups, stages, combinations, anything the API manual lists — so a model can be built from scratch or changed where no plugin tool does it. Look up the table and its fields first with midas_docs_search / midas_docs_read (e.g. "db/ELEM"), and read the current rows with civil_read_table. writes is a list of steps run in order: { table, op: create (POST — new keys only, refused if a key exists) | upsert (PUT — creates or changes; GRUP lists and CNLD/BMLD/PRES/RIGD items MERGE, they are never removed by a PUT) | delete (DESTRUCTIVE — needs allowDestructive; a node takes its elements, an element its loads, a load case its loads), rows: { "<key>": {fields} } | ids: [keys] }. The preview simulates every step over the current model: what each creates, changes (which fields) and deletes; it blocks keys that already exist on create, elements that refer to nodes, materials, sections or thicknesses that do not exist (CIVIL NX accepts a missing section silently), deletes and UNIT / MVCD writes without allowDestructive. Then apply: true with confirmPlanHash writes the steps (stopping at the first refusal), reads every touched row back and reports anything not stored as sent. civil_write_tables_undo puts every touched row back.

table.description: Table key as in the API manual's URI (db/NODE → NODE; LCOM-GEN, MVLDBS…).

additionalProperties.description: One row: the table's fields as the API manual gives them (Assign).

rows.description: create / upsert: { "<key>": { field: value } }, keys are whole numbers.

allowDestructive.description: DESTRUCTIVE: allow delete steps and writes to UNIT / MVCD. Only after the user agreed to what the preview says they do.

apply.description: Write to CIVIL NX. Only after the user approved the preview.

confirmPlanHash.description: planHash from the approved preview; refused if the model or the steps changed.

tools.name: civil_run_analysis
tools.description: Use to run the analysis of any model. For culverts use culvert_analyse_and_check; for PD 6694 SSI use pd6694_ssi_run. Runs the CIVIL NX analysis of the open model (doc/ANAL), so results can be read with the result tools straight after building or changing a model. Replaces the model's results; changes no model data. The model must have been saved to a file at least once (the API cannot analyse an unsaved model): saveFirst: true saves it over its file first. Previews unless apply: true. Can take minutes on a large model.

saveFirst.description: Save the model over its own file before analysing (doc/SAVE).

apply.description: Run it. Only with the user's go-ahead.

tools.name: civil_save_model
tools.description: Use to save the open model, or save it under a new path. Saves the open CIVIL NX model: over its own file (doc/SAVE), or as a new .mcb file when path is given (doc/SAVEAS; a file of that name is overwritten). A model built from scratch must be saved once before it can be analysed. Previews unless apply: true.

path.description: Full Windows path ending in .mcb, e.g. C:\Models\Bridge.mcb. Omit to save over the model's own file.

tools.name: tendon_design
tools.description: Use to design, or check, the prestressing tendons of a concrete girder. It writes nothing: tendon_write does. Designs the post- or pre-tensioning tendons of a concrete girder in the open model to EN 1992-1-1 with the Tendon Designer plugin's own engine, or reads the model's own tendons and checks them (mode improve, the default when tendons run along the girder). Reads the girder (a structure group, element list or the CIVIL NX selection; for improve it is picked from the tendons), its sections, supports and concrete, and the forces: construction-stage results when the model has stages (stage by stage for improve), else the static load cases named, plus an optional live envelope and ULS envelope combination. Creep and shrinkage take the humidity, cement class and drying age from the concrete's time-dependent material, and in mode improve the age at stressing from the construction stages (concreteAge says what was used); forces.prestressFrom civil checks the model's tendons with CIVIL NX's own staged prestress. Span-by-span decks of coupled draped tendons are read as such (no cantilever tendons). The girder is ONE girder line (a group holding several girders is split; girderLine picks one). Composite girders (precast + deck slab) are checked stage by stage (compositeMode) with the slab's own concrete, including the slab top; standard precast beams are pre-tensioned on their published strand positions, with debonded (sleeved) strands set or searched for by debonding, each end's length separately. Then auto-designs the layout (new), reads the tendons in (improve), or takes tendons the user gives as heights above the soffit with transverse distances (soffitTendons, e.g. an existing bridge's tendon schedule), and runs every check: stresses at transfer and in service, Magnel, load balancing, losses, ULS bending, cover, spacing, bend radius, anchorage zones. autoResolve tries the smallest change that clears failed checks. exportSoffitCsv returns the tendons as a soffit-height CSV (download link). The design is kept (designId) for tendon_write. Read-only.

group.description: Structure group holding ONE girder's beam elements - the elements one continuous tendon runs through, end to end (not the whole deck). A group holding several girders is split into its girder lines and one is designed (girderLine).

elementIds.description: The girder's beam elements (one girder line).

useSelection.description: Use the beam elements selected in CIVIL NX (one girder line).

girderLine.description: When the group/elements hold several separate girders: which one to design (1-based, as listed in girderNotes). Default: the one with the most tendons on it.

startNode.description: The girder end its stations are measured from (default: the end the elements run from).

compositeMode.description: Composite girder (precast girder + deck slab section): when the tendons are stressed. before = prestress, girder and wet-slab weight on the girder alone, superimposed dead and live load on the composite section (precast / pre-tensioned); after = the slab has hardened, prestress on the composite section too; off = ignore the slab. Default: worked out from the construction stages (first stressing stage vs the slab's CSCS stage), else before. The slab's concrete is read from the model (CSCS, else the section's Es/Ec).

compositeSection.description: Old name of compositeMode: girder = before, whole = after.

sectionNodeLine.description: Only when CIVIL NX will not send the section records: the node line (top, centroid, bottom) the tendon heights are measured from. Worked out from the model otherwise.

mode.description: new = auto-design new tendons; improve = read the model's own tendons on the girder and check / improve them; given = the tendons in soffitTendons (set automatically when soffitTendons is given). Default: improve when tendons run along the girder, else new.

soffitTendons.description: Tendons given by the user - typically an existing bridge's tendon schedule - as heights of the tendon centre ABOVE THE SOFFIT at stations along the girder, with the transverse distance across the section: the plugin's Heights from soffit… input. Either tendons (each with its points) or csv (the plugin's soffit-height CSV / template: Tendon, Station (m), Height above soffit (mm), Transverse distance y (mm), one row per point; a sheet with stations across also reads). Every check then runs on these tendons as given (no auto-design), and tendon_write can write them. A full-length tendon becomes a spline through its points; a part-length tendon at a constant depth becomes a slab tendon.

transverse_mm.description: Transverse distance from the section centroid, mm (+ as in the plugin's section view), for every point that does not give its own. Default 0.

station_m.description: m from the girder's start (its first node; see startNode).

heightAboveSoffit_mm.description: Height of the tendon centre above the soffit, mm.

transverse_mm.description: Transverse distance at this point, mm (e.g. a tendon in a sloping web).

csv.description: The soffit-height CSV text instead of tendons.

strandsPerTendon.description: Strands per tendon (default: the plugin's default unit, or settings).

exportSoffitCsv.description: Also return the design's tendons (new, improved or given) as the soffit-height CSV - Tendon, Station (m), Height above soffit (mm), Transverse distance y (mm), one row per point - as a download link (soffitHeightsCsv). It is the file the plugin's Heights from soffit… imports and soffitTendons.csv reads.

standardStrands.description: mode new: a section named after a UK/Irish standard precast beam (Y, TY, SY, M, U, W ...) is pre-tensioned on the beam's published strand positions. false (or settings.prestressType "post") post-tensions it instead.

forces.description: Where the forces come from. Default: CIVIL NX - construction-stage results when the model has stages (the construction-stage analysis must have been run), else static load cases.

source.description: beam = no forces read: the plugin's continuous beam with self-weight from the section plus lineLoads.

kind.description: On a staged model: cs (default) or static load cases.

selfWeight.description: Static: self-weight case(s) with their suffix, e.g. ["DL(ST)"]. Default: the case named like self weight / dead.

liveMax.description: Live load envelope max, as CIVIL NX names it, e.g. "LL(MV:max)" or "SLS(CB:max)".

ulsEnvelope.description: A ULS envelope combination used in place of the factored sum.

includesPrestress.description: The combination already holds the prestress secondary moments (default true on a staged model).

prestressFrom.description: mode improve on a staged model: the prestress the checks use. civil = the force, P·e and secondary moment from CIVIL NX's construction-stage results (the real erection sequence, couplers, creep), while the tendons stay as the model has them; plugin = the plugin's own losses and secondary moment on the finished continuous girder. Output prestressInChecks says which was used and why.

lineLoads.description: forces.source beam: superimposed dead and live line loads, kN/m.

losses.description: Loss method and inputs (default EN 1992-1-1 with Annex B creep and shrinkage). code cs455 assesses an existing UK bridge's losses to CS 455 clause 8 (8.7-8.14); the stress limits and resistance checks stay EN 1992-1-1.

loadingAge_days.description: EN 1992: age at loading t0 for creep (default: the age at stressing from the construction stages in mode improve, else 7).

dryingStart_days.description: EN 1992: age drying starts ts, days (default: the model's time-dependent material, else 3).

cementClass.description: EN 1992 cement class (default: the model's time-dependent material, else N).

creepCoefficient.description: EN 1992: a creep coefficient phi(inf, t0) in place of Annex B.

shrinkageAfterStressing_e6.description: EN 1992: the shrinkage strain AFTER stressing, x1e-6, in place of Annex B.

dryingPerimeter.description: EN 1992 h0 = 2Ac/u: outer faces only (default), or with the void faces for vented cells.

hoursOnBed.description: EN 1992 pre-tensioned: hours from tensioning to release (default 24).

psi2.description: Quasi-permanent factor on the traffic (default 0): creep and the relaxation reference stress.

wobbleK_e4.description: Wobble K x1e-4 /m (8.14.4/5: 17 rigid sheaths, at least 33 otherwise; default 33).

elasticShortening.description: 8.11.3: half the modular ratio x the mean stress along the tendon, or (n-1)/2n.

otherLosses_pct.description: Steam curing / other losses, % of the stress at transfer.

fci_MPa.description: Cube strength at transfer (default from the grade and transfer age).

Ec_GPa.description: Concrete modulus at transfer (default Eq 3.5a, 20 + 0.27 fci).

creepPerMPa_e6.description: Creep strain per MPa x1e-6 in place of Table 8.8.3 (0 is used as entered).

shrinkage_e6.description: Shrinkage strain x1e-6 in place of Table 8.9.1 (0 is used as entered).

settings.description: Loads & prestress values that differ from the model / plugin defaults.

fck.description: Concrete grade fck, MPa (default: read from the material).

sigmaJack.description: Jacking stress, MPa (default 1395, or the model tendons' own).

stressing.description: Jacked from both ends, the start or the end (improve: default as in the model).

strandTendons.description: Pre-tensioned: how strands become CIVIL NX tendons. group (default) = strands treated alike (top / bottom face, deflected, debonded length) are one tendon of n strands; level = one per row and treatment; each = one tendon per strand. Forces and resultant are the same; design.strandTendonsInCivil lists them.

transferAge_days.description: Age of the concrete when the tendons are stressed, days: fck(t), the transfer stress limits and the anchorage strength (default: from the construction stages in mode improve - the youngest element - else 7).

strandUnits.description: new: strands per tendon to try (default 7, 12, 15, 19, 22, 27, 31).

maxTendonsPerColumn.description: new: tendons per web column at most (default 4).

transferLength.description: Post-tensioned transfer length (default calc, in the checks). calc = each tendon's own length from EN 1992-1-1 8.10.3(5) (spread at 2 beta, beta = arctan 2/3, from the bearing plate to the top/soffit and across its share of the width); user = begin_m / end_m for every tendon; none = full force at the anchor; auto = CIVIL NX's 0.5 x (H + Bf/n). tendon_write writes it (calc and user as user defined). inChecks (default true): the design's checks build each tendon's force up linearly over it, as CIVIL NX does; false = full force at the anchor in the checks.

debonding.description: Pre-tensioned only: strands sleeved (debonded) at the beam ends so they carry no force there - relieves transfer tension at the ends. "auto" = the plugin's Find debonding on the strands as designed (pairs of inner strands, 1-6 m, within 25 % of all strands and 40 % of a row, outermost strands bonded; taken only if checks improve); "none" = every strand bonded (auto-design does not debond either); or a list giving exactly the strands to sleeve, by name as design.debonding.strandNames lists them (standard positions like "A.5", or tendon numbers on a tendon grid). Omitted: as auto-design left it (on a standard precast beam it may already debond). Written to CIVIL NX as each strand's DeBondBLEN / DeBondELEN.

endA_m.description: Sleeved length at end A (the girder's start), m.

externalTendons.description: mode new, post-tensioned box or U girders: add external tendons in the void (CIVIL NX External tendon type), straight between deviators - anchored at the centroid, low at 0.3 and 0.7 of each span just clear of the bottom slab, high over interior supports. Added before the internal tendons are sized, so those are sized with them in place.

count.description: External tendons (placed beside each web; one at the middle when odd).

mu.description: Friction at the deviators (default 0.12, HDPE duct, EN 1992-1-1 Table 5.1; steel 0.25).

clear_mm.description: Clear gap from the sheath to the concrete, mm (default 50).

columnStrands.description: Strands per tendon, column by column (left to right, as design.columns lists them); null = the design's strandsPerTendon. A column with its own count is written with its own tendon property. Post-tensioned draped tendons only (not standard strand patterns).

search.description: mode new: how hard to look for the layout. Pre-tensioned standard beam + deep = the plugin's strand search run to the time limit (strand counts, top strands, jacking stress, debonding and deflected strands, then the neighbours of the best layouts refined strand by strand). Post-tensioned: fast (default, seconds) = the plugin's quick search, every tendon on one shared profile. deep = the plugin's Find the best layout - Deep: every arrangement (strands per tendon x tendons per column), each on one shared profile AND with a profile per mirrored pair of columns (outer webs, inner webs ... each with its own low points, levels over the piers and anchors), hundreds to thousands of profiles sampled then refined span by span; returns the chosen layout plus the best option of each arrangement (autoDesign.deep.options). Use deep when the user wants the best / most economical layout or tendons profiled individually.

options.description: deep: options listed (the best of each arrangement).

balance.description: deep only: load balancing as the aim, as the plugin's Load balancing + Deep. Passing layouts that balance target % of the chosen load in EVERY span (within ±5 points) are ranked first, then the least strand; otherwise the closest. The aim never overrides a failing check. Each option reports its balance per span.

load.description: permanent = self-weight + superimposed dead (final force); self = self-weight; girder = self-weight + wet slab; transfer = load at transfer (force at transfer).

target.description: Target, % of that load balanced in each span.

autoResolve.description: When checks fail, try the smallest change that clears them (the plugin's Auto-resolve); taken only if fewer checks fail.

keep.description: autoResolve: what it must not change. improve default: anchors, count, strandsPerTendon and duct kept, profile free; new default: nothing kept.

tools.name: tendon_write
tools.description: Use after tendon_design, to write its tendons into the model. Writes a tendon_design result into the open model with the Tendon Designer plugin's writer: the strand material and tendon property (or one already in the model), every tendon profile (TDNA) and its prestress (TDPL) in the prestress load case, one load group per tendon group, and - when a construction stage is named - each group's load group activated in its stage. With improve, the model's own tendons the design was read from are removed first (only while unchanged since). Refused when the model, the girder, or the loads the forces were read from changed, and while checks fail unless allowFailedChecks. The model is re-checked before writing, the journal is kept before the first change, and every row is read back. Previews unless apply: true.

designId.description: The tendon_design result to write (default: the latest).

prefix.description: Tendon name prefix, at most 8 characters (tendons are named <prefix>-C1R1, ...).

loadCase.description: Prestress load case (default PS, or the model tendons' own).

loadGroupPrefix.description: Each tendon group's prestress goes in a load group named this prefix plus the group's name (made if missing). Empty string = no load group (Default); stages need one.

stage.description: Activate every tendon group's load group in this construction stage.

stages.description: Per tendon group (its key or label from tendon_design design.groups): the construction stage it is stressed in.

replace.description: Remove tendons this tool wrote before on these elements with the same prefix (recorded in the ledger and unchanged since).

tendonPropertyId.description: Use this tendon property already in the model (default: the model tendons' own for improve, else a new one from the design). null = a new one.

strandMaterialId.description: Strand material already in the model for a new tendon property (default: a new strand material).

transferLength.description: Post-tensioned transfer length written to each profile. Omitted: the design's own (tendon_design settings.transferLength, default calc = each tendon's EN 1992-1-1 8.10.3(5) length, written as user defined). calc / user (begin, end in m) / none (full force at the anchor) / auto (CIVIL NX's 0.5 x (H + Bf/n)).

allowFailedChecks.description: Write a design whose checks fail. Only with the user's agreement.

tools.name: ec2_describe_section
tools.description: Step 1 of an EN 1992 (Eurocode) concrete section check. For CS 455 use cs455_describe_section; only to read or edit a section's shape use section_read. Start here for an EN 1992 section check. Reads one beam section of the open model through the shared MIDAS section library (any CIVIL NX section family; composite deck slabs as separate regions; tapered sections per end), places the bars from the given schedule with the Eurocode Section Checker's own placement and, for a prestressed beam, the tendons - and RETURNS A DRAWING of the section with every bar and tendon. Compare it with the user's drawing and correct rebar / psc.tendons until they match, then call ec2_section_check. Also returns depth, width, area, the bars placed per schedule row (or why a row failed), the concrete class read from the model material and the member type / length the model suggests. An unknown sectionId is answered with the model's beam sections. Read-only.

tools.name: ec2_section_check
tools.description: Use for EN 1992 checks of RC or prestressed beam, column, pier or pile sections. For CS 455 use cs455_assess; for slabs and plates use slab_assess; for a stress plot use stress_profile. EN 1992-1-1 / EN 1992-2 check of concrete beam, column, pier and pile sections with the Eurocode Section Checker plugin's own engine. Reads the concurrent force sets at the chosen stations for the chosen combinations (BEAMFORCE for plain combinations; BEAMFORCEVBM for envelopes and moving loads, with the concurrency guard - a combination with no concurrent sets is checked at the corners of its force box, never mixed), then checks every row: ULS biaxial bending with axial force (fibre section), shear Vz and Vy (6.2), torsion (6.3), detailing; SLS stresses (7.2) and crack width (7.3) under characteristic / quasi-permanent rows; columns and piles to 5.8 (slenderness, imperfections, nominal curvature). Prestressed beams (psc): transfer stresses, stage-by-stage stresses with the girder alone and the composite section, ULS with the tendons' strain, shear with prestress, interface shear (6.2.5), decompression and crack width (Table 7.1N / 7.101N). Returns the verdict, the governing row of every check per section, the worst rows and what was not covered. Read-only; a job on the website.

tools.name: undo_run
tools.description: Use to reverse any change a tool made to the model (list the recorded runs, preview, then apply). For wind or PD 6694 loads use ec_wind_remove / pd6694_route_a_remove / pd6694_ssi_remove; to take out loads or supports added by hand use civil_remove_loads. Reverses one change a tool made to the model, from the record every apply leaves. Without runId it lists the recent runs (newest first) with what each changed; with runId it previews the undo (what will be deleted or restored) and writes nothing; with runId and apply: true it reverses that run, using the undo of the tool that made it. Undo later work before the model it sits on. Wind loads and PD 6694 loads are taken out with ec_wind_remove / pd6694_route_a_remove / pd6694_ssi_remove instead; the list says so.

runId.description: The run to reverse, from the list undo_run gives without runId (or from the apply's result).

apply.description: false (default): preview the undo. true: reverse the run.

force.description: Bridge Reshaper and Bridge Thermal Loads only: undo even though the model changed since the run (their preview says when this is needed).

tidy.description: Beam to Plate only: also delete nodes left unused.
